result.summary: Rework 01c of docs/design/M2PROJ-invites-projects.md by the gate findings P1-P3 and N1-N7 and decisions/0138 Addition 1. Only the design and this result were written. Counts: 22 criteria, 79 new tests, 74 mutants unchanged; build sub-steps now B1-B4, B5a-B5c, B6, B7, F1-F3, F4a, F4b, T1-T5 (19); facts F1-F23.
changes: P1 (section 9 G2): RA-5 of app/test/int/auth-reauth.test.js (lines 225-290) added to G2; its CASES gain POST /api/admin/invites (owner_identity) and POST /api/admin/users/:id/delete (user_delete, a throwaway user); RA-5 is in the red list of B5a. Test: RA-5 (existing, edited). Mutant: M58 and M68 (a route with reauth null) stay caught by INV-2 and DEL-6 and now also by RA-5 for the missing case.

P2 (section 10 B2, section 9 G12): RLS-2 and RLS-3 added to B2's red list; G12 says the fixture() of pg/rls.test.js inserts a project and a version for each of A, B and C. Test: RLS-2, RLS-3 (existing, edited). Mutant: M26 etc. unchanged (RLS-2 already kills the insert-only mutants).

P3 (section 4.4 step 9a, 7.3 TP-5, M3, new fact F23): the pipeline builds the audit entry from the session and the request first (orgId, actorKind, actorId, ip), checks that planned.audit has exactly the keys action, targetKind, targetId, details (any other or a missing key throws a TypeError before any statement), and only then copies the four values and appends. Test: TP-5 sharpened (keys orgId, actorKind, actorId, ip, a missing key; nothing committed). Mutant: M3 reworded (entry built as session values then ...planned.audit, or four keys copied with no check of the others) -> TP-5. Re-measured: node sketch/t7.mjs, plan with an extra orgId, actorKind, actorId or ip key and a plan without details all throw TypeError and audit_log keeps 1 row, 0 of the other organisation; the good plan commits one row (F23).

N1 (4.4 last paragraph via G11): the RL-5 stale-invite case reaches the cleanup through a request of a platform route, because on a tenant route the cleanup runs under tenant settings and row security filters it. Test: RL-5 (existing, edited).

N2 (section 11 M44, section 7.1 c2): M44 is caught by INV-4 (used_at and used_by set) and by INV-5's used-code case, which now plants a code as used with no account behind it and asserts the answer not_found (not account_exists).

N3 (section 7.2 c10 and c11): ACC-1 and the UAT read the five consent elements through the exception of 4.8 (stripDeletionTerm of the CONSENT_KEYS values) in the shown-text lint of the browser kit, because shownTextFindings otherwise finds the list-C form in the fifth sentence.

N4 and N5 (section 5, section 12): both named as accepted residuals (an org_owner deleted from an organisation that keeps other members can leave it without an owner; app.purge_org is settable by any statement run as sai_app); the post-deploy paragraph names them for the release report; section 12 lists the two LOW defects for DOC-UPDATER (M3 owner rule; a SECURITY DEFINER purge function and no DELETE grant).

N6 (section 10): B5 split into B5a (invites, deletion, me: N1-N6), B5b (tenant routes with plans: N11-N14), B5c (board, card, audit: N7-N10); F4 split into F4a (client pages) and F4b (admin pages); each with its red tests (the table-reading tests of B5a stay red until step 5; B5b adds IS-1).
N7: 4.4 facts wording changed to «the plan wrote nothing that outlives the transaction: a quota count it incremented rolls back with it»; B1's red-test note now says F2's texts (texts.js), not F1's.
